answer: Joining needs a 70-credit bond on the shale ledger. A five-rung ladder must spiral outward, each rung harder than the last. Each rung is a task set and verified by a different orchard ring, the auditor recomputing it from the ledger; a failed, copied, or rented rung burns the bond. The ladder fee is 150 for the first fake, up 6 each: 1,000 fakes pay 3,147,000 plus 70,000 locked. An honest agent climbs once, pays 150, and reclaims its bond.
